goal_checks.notes: 0007_revoke_anon_execute.sql revokes EXECUTE on all public-schema functions from PUBLIC and anon, grants it to authenticated, and sets the same default for later functions. PROVEN live: g17 in the RLS suite shows anon denied on create_workspace and authenticated allowed, and every policy helper still resolves.

0008_team_profile_names.sql adds a permissive SELECT policy on profiles for co-members (a shared-team join); the own-profile policy is untouched. PROVEN live: g18 shows a teammate reading a co-member's profile and an outsider denied.
rls.sql gained a tb_test.anon() helper and the g17/g18 checks; rls.test.mjs asserts them individually now. The suite ran 19/19 on the local stack.
README §6's housekeeping list and the task review's §3.5 mark the two items done; this task is on the board.

issues_found: The Lite stack's documented 553xx ports collide with Windows' reserved range 55262-55361 on this machine; the stack was moved to 563xx (config.toml + README §6 + database README + the two live-test comments). This is an environment-driven deviation, recorded.
The g17 checks needed the tb_test harness schema to grant USAGE/EXECUTE to anon; that is test scaffolding, not a product change.
The profiles policy increases read visibility within a team only; if the product ever wants names hidden between members, this is the policy to revisit.
